ask: Go 1.22, standard library only. main.go: net/http JSON API with middleware chain (request id, structured logging with slog, panic recovery, simple token auth), two handlers with typed request/response structs, graceful shutdown on SIGTERM with context timeouts. write the file.
prose:
The file was written but I used `github.com/google/uuid` — that breaks the "standard library only" constraint. Rewriting with a crypto/rand-based UUID v4.Done. `main.go` is clean stdlib only — `crypto/rand` for UUID v4, `log/slog` for structured JSON logging, and the middleware chain wires up in order: request ID → structured logger → panic recovery → token auth.

A few things worth knowing:

- Middleware order matters here. `requestID` runs first so the generated ID is available to every later middleware via context. `structuredLogger` wraps the downstream call so it captures the final status code after the handler runs.
- Token auth reads `API_TOKEN` from the environment. Empty string disables it — handy for local dev, just don't forget to set it elsewhere.
- The `responseWriter` wrapper is necessary because `http.ResponseWriter` doesn't expose the status code after the fact — without it the logger would always log 200.
- Graceful shutdown gives in-flight requests 15 seconds to complete before the process exits. Adjust that constant to taste.

To run:

```bash
go run main.go
# with auth:
API_TOKEN=secret go run main.go

# test status
curl http://localhost:8080/status

# test create user
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/users \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"Alice","email":"alice@example.com"}'
```
